data.narrative:
Atomic Machines is a Series A-stage semiconductor company that has raised $144M to date. The valuation assessment draws from a private comp universe of 8 frontier semiconductor businesses at similar stages, supplemented by reference to 3 public semiconductor peers (ALAB, NVDA, AMD) trading at a median 18.4x price-to-sales.

Two triangulation methods are applicable. Stage-progression analysis applies a 2.0x step-up multiplier to the $144M raised proxy, implying a $288M valuation. Peer-median analysis anchors to three same-stage, same-sector comparables—SambaNova Systems ($11.0B), Rebellions ($2.3B), and d-Matrix ($2.0B)—yielding a median valuation of $2.3B, with a range of $2.0B to $11.0B. Public-comp anchoring via EV/Revenue is not applicable because Atomic Machines does not disclose revenue, a standard limitation for private-stage companies.

Synthesizing the two applicable methods produces a valuation range of $245M (low) to $2.7B (high), with a median of $1.3B. The wide dispersion reflects material uncertainty around the company's technical differentiation and near-term commercialization trajectory. The stage-progression method produces the conservative bound; the peer-median method dominates the center and upper range. Resolution of this range hinges on capital efficiency relative to peers, product-market validation progress, and whether the company's positioning aligns more closely with development-stage entrants or nearer-to-revenue competitors like SambaNova.
